## PNEUMOCYSTIS JIROVECII PROPHYLAXIS (PCP Prophylaxis)
Indications for primary prophylaxis of P. jirovecii include:
1) HIV/AIDS patients with CD4 count <200 cells/microliter
2) Hematopoietic or organ transplantation patients during immunosuppression
3) Patients receiving Alemtuzumab, temozolomide or fludarabine
4) Patients receiving >/= 20mg equivalent of prednisone per day for over 1 month
5) Patients with acute lymphocytic leukemia, rheumatologic disease receiving
immunosuppressive therapy and certain primary immunodeficiencies (e.g. severe
combined immunodeficiency, idiopathic CD4 T-lymphocytopenia, hyper-IgM
syndrome)
Dose and duration of prophylaxis varies with the indication. Please contact
Infectious Diseases or Hematology/Oncology for more information.
Prophylaxis should be discontinued when host defenses are restored. In persons
with AIDS on highly active antiretroviral therapy, Prophylaxis should be
discontinued when the CD4 cell concentrations remain over 200 cells/microliter
for 3 to 6 months in patients, except that prophylaxis should be continued for
life in those who have had P. jirovecii disease.
## Recommended FIRST-LINE prophylaxis:
[Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet q day ($) [R,DI]](psjzid-trimeth-sulfa-1-ds-tablet-po-q24h)
< OR >
[Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 1 SS tablet q day ($) [R,DI]](psjzid-trimeth-sulfa-ss-q24h)
## Alternative when trimethoprim/sulfa is poorly tolerated or contraindicated:
**Patient should be tested for glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6-PD)
deficiency before starting dapsone. Individuals deficient in G6-PD
show about a 2-fold increase in sensitivity toward dapsone-induced hemolytic
anemia.
G6-PD lab test are resulted the same day or next day. May be add on lab.
G6-PD lab result should be "normal" to start dapsone therapy.
[[Click here] G6-PD Screen Lab Order](lrtz-g6-pd-screen)
[Dapsone 100mg PO q day ($) [DI]](psjzid-dapsone-100mg-po-qday-pcp-prophlaxis)

## Atovaquone is alternative for patient for clinical reason:
(e.g. patients with SLE, hematologic concerns, G6PD deficiency)
